NAT GATEWAY COST ADVISOR · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Is your NAT gateway bill avoidable?

Paste one row per NAT gateway and destination — GB per month to S3, DynamoDB, ECR, CloudWatch Logs, anything — and get what the NAT gateway costs, the free S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints you are missing, the interface endpoints that beat $0.045/GB after their hourly fee, the idle gateways and the ready-to-paste aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint commands.

Nothing is uploaded and AWS is never contacted. The text box is analysed in this browser and never leaves your device. The GB per destination is the number you supply, so traffic you did not label counts as internet.

Prefer a CLI, or want a CI check?

Same logic, zero dependencies, one command — reads a file or stdin:

node cli.mjs analyze nat.csv
cat nat.csv | node cli.mjs analyze -
node cli.mjs analyze nat.csv --azs 3 --region eu-west-1

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: NAT gateway vs VPC endpoint: what it costs and when to switch.

What's recognised

InputHandling

Prices are illustrative and dated; edit them with --prices in the CLI. Other regions, cross-AZ data transfer, data transfer out to the internet, endpoint policies and PrivateLink services outside AWS are not modelled.

Common questions

Does this connect to my AWS account?

No. It reads the rows you paste and never contacts AWS. It cannot see your real invoice, Savings Plans, private pricing or free tier, so every dollar figure is the rows you pasted times list prices you can edit.

How do I get the GB per destination?

Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the NAT gateway's network interface and sum bytes by destination, or in Cost Explorer filter usage type NatGateway-Bytes by gateway. Label the destinations you can tell are AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, ECR, CloudWatch Logs, STS, SSM); everything else counts as internet and is never recommended for an endpoint.

Why is S3 through a NAT gateway such a common waste?

A NAT gateway charges $0.045 per GB processed for every byte, including bytes to S3 in the same region, while a gateway endpoint for S3 or DynamoDB is free and is only a route-table entry. Terabytes of S3 reads from private subnets cost hundreds of dollars a month for nothing.

When is an interface endpoint worth it?

An interface endpoint costs $0.01 per hour per AZ (about $7.30 a month per AZ) plus $0.01 per GB, against $0.045 per GB through the NAT gateway. It breaks even at roughly 209 GB a month per endpoint per AZ, and services such as ECR, SSM and ECS need two or three endpoints, which the tool counts.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The browser page analyses the text in your own browser and never sends it anywhere. The CLI reads a local file or stdin and makes no network call.

nat-gateway-vs-vpc-endpoint-cost.html.text:
NAT Gateway Cost Advisor · guide

NAT gateway vs VPC endpoint: what it costs and when to switch

Short answer: send S3 and DynamoDB traffic through free gateway endpoints, and put an interface endpoint in front of any other AWS service that moves more than a few hundred GB a month. Everything else on the NAT gateway is the price of reaching the internet from a private subnet.

What a NAT gateway costs (us-east-1 list prices, illustrative)

  • Hourly: $0.045 per gateway-hour, about $32.85 a month, whether or not anything uses it.
  • Public IPv4: $0.005 per hour for the address, about $3.65 a month.
  • Processing: $0.045 per GB in either direction, for every destination, including AWS services in the same region.

What the alternatives cost

  • Gateway endpoint (S3, DynamoDB): free. It is a route-table entry, with no hourly fee and no per-GB fee.
  • Interface endpoint (most other services): $0.01 per hour per AZ (about $7.30 a month per AZ) plus $0.01 per GB. Break-even against the NAT gateway is about 209 GB a month per endpoint per AZ.
  • Services that need several endpoints: ECR needs ecr.api and ecr.dkr (plus the free S3 gateway endpoint for image layers); SSM needs ssm, ssmmessages and ec2messages; ECS needs ecs, ecs-agent and ecs-telemetry. The fixed fee multiplies, and so does the break-even.
  • IPv6: outbound IPv6 through an egress-only internet gateway has no per-GB processing fee.

Find the avoidable spend

  1. Get GB per destination: VPC Flow Logs on the NAT gateway's network interface summed by destination, or Cost Explorer usage type NatGateway-Bytes by gateway.
  2. Write one row per gateway and destination: nat-0a1,s3,4200.
  3. Paste into the advisor, or run node cli.mjs analyze nat.csv. It prints a create-vpc-endpoint command for each endpoint that saves money.
  4. Create the endpoint in one VPC first. A gateway endpoint adds routes to the route tables you name; an interface endpoint with private DNS changes where the service name resolves, and its security group must allow 443 from the VPC.

Questions

How much does a NAT gateway cost?

In us-east-1 a NAT gateway costs $0.045 per hour (about $32.85 a month) plus $0.045 for every GB it processes, in either direction, plus $0.005 per hour (about $3.65 a month) for its public IPv4 address. Three gateways, one per AZ, cost about $110 a month before any traffic.

Is S3 traffic through a NAT gateway charged?

Yes. The NAT gateway charges $0.045 per GB for every byte it processes, including bytes to S3 in the same region. A gateway endpoint for S3 is free, so moving that traffic to it removes the charge. The same is true for DynamoDB.

Do VPC endpoints cost money?

Gateway endpoints (S3 and DynamoDB) are free. Interface endpoints cost $0.01 per hour per AZ plus $0.01 per GB processed, so they only beat the NAT gateway's $0.045 per GB above a break-even volume of about 209 GB a month per endpoint per AZ.
